$comment: Which screens the visual suite captures, and which design references are still waiting for one. A reference in `mockups/` that appears in neither list fails the suite by name, so a design cannot arrive and be forgotten. A screen whose status is `baselined` must have a committed baseline and an acceptance record naming the reference it was first reviewed against — that record is what turns 'the console matches the design' from an intention into something the gate holds, because after the first acceptance ordinary visual regression keeps it matched. `viewport` and `theme` are how one route becomes several screens: the design declares three widths and two themes, and a baseline that only ever saw one of them proves nothing about the other five.

accepted.reason: The first screen the toolchain had to prove itself against. It is not one of the designed screens — it renders the run list with no design system behind it — so there is no reference to review it against, and it is expected to be replaced rather than restyled.

The colour section renders every role pair with the ratio computed from the token table, and every status with its documented shape. Reviewed side by side against the reference: the values match to the byte and the shapes match the seven documented states.

The same geometry under the dark token set. The browser suite asserts the stronger form of this claim — every box, to the pixel, identical between the two themes — and this baseline is the picture of it.

The scale section renders the type, spacing, radius, border and duration scales as the closed sets the reference documents. Reviewed against it: eight type steps, seven spacing steps, four radii, and no additional step in any of them.

The middle breakpoint in the dark token set. There is no reference for this combination — the design documents three widths and two themes but draws one picture of each — so this baseline exists to catch a regression rather than to record a review.

The empty and error states, at the narrowest width the console declares. Reviewed against the reference: icon, one-line heading, one sentence saying what would be here, and an action, in that order, with the error state naming its dependency in monospace.
The narrowest width in the dark token set. As with the 768 dark capture there is no reference for the combination, so this baseline catches a regression rather than recording a review.

mockups.note: The colour token table and its contrast pairs. Baselined by the gallery route rather than by a product screen, because the token table is not something any product screen shows.
Spacing, type and radius scales. Same gallery route, captured at the middle breakpoint.
One investigation, live: transcript, evidence and the decisions waiting on a person.
The empty, error and loading states every surface reuses. They are primitives rather than a screen, so the gallery is where they are reviewed.
The dark theme: the same token names at different values and identical geometry. Reviewed against the gallery in dark rather than against a product screen, because what it documents is the token set.
